summary:
Our project, ASTRIS (Autonomous Spaceflight Triage & Responsive Intervention System), is designed to help astronauts monitor their health and respond to potential medical risks during space missions.

We developed an offline first health monitoring and decision support system that monitors astronaut health and environmental conditions, identifies potential risks, classifies their severity, and provides alerts with recommended intervention steps.

The main challenge we address is that astronauts cannot always receive immediate medical support from Earth due to communication delays or blackouts. They also face health risks such as radiation exposure, cardiovascular problems, bone and muscle loss, fatigue, and environmental changes.

ASTRIS helps address these challenges by performing onboard health assessments and providing guidance without depending on a continuous internet connection. Even during communication blackouts, health checks and warnings remain active, and data is stored locally until communication is restored.

We also integrated real public NASA data through NASA DONKI and NASA POWER for space-weather and solar irradiance information.

This project is important because astronaut safety should not depend entirely on communication with Earth. Our goal is to provide faster health-risk awareness and reliable onboard support, making future long-duration space missions safer.
details: Our project, ASTRIS, is an offline first astronaut health monitoring and decision support system. It monitors health and environmental conditions, identifies potential risks, classifies their severity, and provides alerts with recommended actions. We used React, TypeScript, Express.js, Recharts, browser localStorage, and NASA DONKI and POWER APIs. Its biggest benefit is that it can continue health assessments and store data even when communication with Earth is unavailable. What makes it creative is combining multiple health monitoring areas, NASA data, risk detection, and offline functionality in one platform. Our goal is to improve astronaut safety and support future long duration space missions. We also considered reliability, ease of use, data security, and the different health risks astronauts face.
